briefing.summary: Markets open Monday in a fragile, range-bound posture following a violent volatility unwind — VIX crushed 12.5% Friday but remains elevated at 18.12, while the S&P sits near 52-week lows with a deeply inverted yield curve and extreme fear readings. The narrative is split: international markets (Nikkei +3.45%, DAX +0.48%) and a falling dollar suggest some risk appetite returning globally, yet domestic breadth is catastrophically weak (0% of stocks above 200 DMA) and small caps are lagging badly, warning that the recovery is shallow and concentrated. With CPI just 2 days away and the regime flagging low confidence range-bound conditions, the disciplined posture today is observation over action.

sections.title: 1. Overall Market Posture & Regime
sections.content: The regime classifier lands on RANGE-BOUND with only 36% confidence — itself a signal. The S&P is flat on the session but sits near 52-week lows after a punishing 20-day drawdown of -5.09%, recovering only 3.05% over the last 5 days. That bounce is narrow: the Russell 2000 is -0.91% Friday and lagging growth by 2.46% over 5 days, a classic 'relief rally in large caps only' signature. Fear & Greed at 0 (extreme fear) alongside VIX at 18.12 — still above the 16-17 complacency zone — means the market is not yet in a clean recovery. The stress reading of 16/100 and risk appetite of 45/100 reinforce a no-man's-land environment. The minimum conviction threshold is raised to 78 today with -5 penalties on both longs and shorts. The regime is explicitly saying: do less, not more.

sections.title: 2. Sector Rotation & Relative Strength
sections.content: Friday's sector tape tells a clear story: this is a tech/momentum-led defensive bounce, not a broad risk-on rotation. Semis (SMH +0.94%) and Tech (XLK +0.82%) are the only real winners, consistent with the Nasdaq outperforming the Russell. Energy (XLE +0.49%) adds a commodity-adjacent bid. Meanwhile, the typical risk-on sectors are ALL in the red — Financials (-0.52%), Industrials (-0.51%), Discretionary (-0.40%), and Materials (-0.44%) are all down. This is notable: Discretionary is a regime overweight due to lower gas prices, yet it's lagging. Real Estate (-0.60%) and Comm Services (-0.69%) lead the losers, both rate-sensitive or sentiment-driven names struggling under an inverted curve and cautious positioning. The rotation picture says: growth tech is a safe haven here, not a risk-on leader. Airlines are a regime overweight on fuel cost tailwinds — WTI at $78.35 and falling (-2.14%) supports that thesis structurally, though today's price action needs validation.

sections.title: 3. Yield Curve & Rate Signals
sections.content: The yield curve remains deeply inverted on two measures: 2-10 spread at -24bps and 3M-10Y at a stark -116bps. The 10Y yield fell 84bps to 3.91% — a significant single-day move into the weekend — signaling a bond market that is pricing meaningful rate cuts and/or recession risk. This is not a growth-positive yield move; it is a flight-to-quality bid. The term structure for VIX is in contango, which is mildly stabilizing for equities (near-term fear not spiking), but the absolute level of inversion on rates is incompatible with a sustained equity recovery in rate-sensitive sectors. With CPI in 2 days (Wednesday), any upside surprise reignites the rate fear trade and could shatter the fragile 3-day bounce. The bond market is pricing more aggressively for cuts than the equity market has fully reflected — that divergence is the week's key tension.

sections.title: 4. Currency & Commodity Flows
sections.content: Dollar weakness (-0.56% to 102.56) is a meaningful data point: it helped fuel the international outperformance (Nikkei +3.45% — largely a carry-unwind reversal, DAX +0.48%, FTSE +0.30%, EM names positive) and provided a tailwind for commodities priced in USD. However, Gold only gained +0.17% despite dollar weakness, suggesting gold is not in a panic-bid mode — consistent with the stress reading of 16/100. Oil's -2.14% drop to $78.35 is a double-edged signal: bullish for consumer and airline names (lower input costs), but bearish for Energy equities unless seen as demand-destruction. USD/JPY at 146.98 bears watching — the yen carry unwind that drove last week's volatility spike is not fully resolved at this level, and any drop toward 144-145 could reignite equity vol. Bitcoin +2.11% adds a mild risk-appetite signal but Ethereum's -0.76% divergence suggests crypto is not in a unified risk-on mode.

sections.title: 5. Key Risk Factors Into the Week
sections.content: Five risks warrant active monitoring: (1) CPI Wednesday — the dominant binary event; a hot print resets the rate-cut narrative and breaks the bounce. (2) USD/JPY stability — yen carry unwind remains an unresolved systemic risk; a move below 145 could spike VIX back above 25. (3) Breadth failure — 0% of S&P names above 200 DMA is an extraordinary reading; if the rally cannot broaden from Semis/Tech to Financials and Industrials this week, the bounce fails. (4) Small cap divergence — Russell underperformance of 1.02pp signals liquidity preference and credit concern; HY spreads at 109.9bps are tight but IG showing -19.88bps compression suggests credit is not in crisis mode yet. (5) OPEX week dynamics — options expiration can amplify moves intraday; combined with a low-conviction regime and elevated VIX, gamma effects may create whipsaw conditions unsuitable for directional positioning.

scenarios.condition: If CPI prints in-line or below (core ≤0.2% MoM) on Wednesday
scenarios.implication: Rate-cut narrative solidifies, 10Y yields drop further, dollar weakens more. Tech/Growth leadership accelerates. Discretionary and airlines could finally activate as overweights. VIX likely drops toward 15-16.
scenarios.trade: Hold off initiating until CPI prints. If cool, look for SMH/XLK continuation and airline names (JETS ETF) on the open Wednesday. Regime penalty still applies — wait for 78+ conviction setups.

scenarios.implication: The 3-day bounce is immediately at risk. Rate-cut timeline pushed out, 10Y back toward 4.1-4.2%, dollar rebounds, VIX spikes. The extreme fear reading at F&G=0 means capitulation positioning — a hot print could trigger forced selling.
scenarios.trade: Defensive posture: inverse tech or S&P hedges could work but carry -5 conviction penalty. Better to be flat and re-evaluate post-CPI. Do not chase the bounce into the print.

scenarios.event: Yen Carry Unwind Resumption (USD/JPY watching 145 level)

scenarios.condition: If USD/JPY breaks below 145 during Monday-Tuesday session
scenarios.implication: Risk-off cascade similar to the Aug 5 episode could resurface. VIX would likely spike back above 22-25. International equity correlations break down as Japanese institutions repatriate. The Nikkei's +3.45% Friday bounce reverses.
scenarios.trade: No new longs. Consider VIX call spreads or SPY puts as tail hedges. Gold may finally catch a real bid. This is a scenario to survive, not trade aggressively.

scenarios.condition: If USD/JPY holds 147-148 range through the week
scenarios.implication: Carry unwind stabilizes, global risk appetite normalizes, international outperformance continues. The dollar weakness tailwind persists for multinationals and EM.
scenarios.trade: EEM or international ETFs (EFA) become attractive on a CPI confirmation. Not actionable today given regime conviction hurdle.

scenarios.event: Breadth Recovery Test (Can the rally broaden beyond Tech?)

scenarios.condition: If Financials (XLF), Industrials (XLI), and Small Caps (IWM) join the bid early this week
scenarios.implication: Breadth improvement would be the single most bullish signal possible from this setup. A move of XLF +1%+ and IWM closing the gap with QQQ would suggest the bounce has legs and regime could shift toward bullish with higher confidence.
scenarios.trade: IWM long on breadth confirmation, targeting the 5-day recovery range. Still apply conviction filter — only enter if setup clears 78+ threshold after regime penalties.

scenarios.condition: If Tech/Semis continue to rally alone while Financials and Industrials stay red
scenarios.implication: The current narrow rally is a dead-cat structure. Smart money rotating to tech as defensive growth, not risk-on positioning. The S&P will struggle to reclaim 200 DMA and the range-bound regime persists or worsens.
scenarios.trade: No new longs. Consider sector-relative pairs (long XLK / short XLF) if conviction allows, but the -5 penalty on both sides makes this difficult to clear 78. Default to cash.
